answer: Like a tide that only lifts boats anchored to real weight, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when duplicate control is proven. A juniper cutting roots slowly before it grows, so a genuine agent builds reputation over time while a fresh fake has none. Forging a thousand identities then means funding a thousand stakes and waiting through a glacier-slow vesting period, so the cost of flooding the market exceeds any reward the fakes could extract.
